verifiedBy: npm dist-tags.latest on registry.npmjs.org (0.4.1) cross-read against the git tag of the same version (`git show v0.4.1:cmd/litespm/main.go` → parseInstallFlags)
_readme: What a reader actually installs. `npx --yes litespm@latest` resolves to this
version, so these are the only install flags the site may publish — the
flags a reader's binary accepts is a property of npm, not of this working
tree. That distinction is what let the site publish `--agent` and
`--all-detected` while the published CLI rejected both.
scripts/check-install-command.mjs reads this file, asks npm for the live
dist-tag when it can, and fails when they disagree — so publishing a new
release cannot silently leave this file (and therefore the site) behind.
Update `version` and `installFlags` together: parse them from the tag you
just published with the same `case "--flag"` read the gate performs.
